title: BEEM: Boosting Performance of Early Exit DNNs using Multi-Exit Classifiers as Experts

contributions.purpose: Improve early-exit (EE) inference by better using information across exits, since prior EE criteria (confidence-based, patience/voting-based) treat every exit classifier equally and discard confidence from previous layers.
contributions.mechanism: BEEM: treat each intermediate exit classifier as an expert (ensemble learning). Aggregate weighted confidence scores of consecutive previous exits whose predictions agree with the current exit (deeper exits weighted higher by accuracy/cost); on disagreement, reset to the current exit's score. A sample exits when the aggregated confidence exceeds a threshold.
contributions.evaluation: On GLUE (language tasks) and COCO (image captioning): speed-up of 1.5x-2.1x over final-layer inference; accuracy comparable to final layer on harder image captioning and improved on easier language tasks. Outperforms SOTA EE methods in both speed and accuracy.
contributions.domain: Efficient inference / adaptive early-exit for transformer DNNs
contributions.source_quote: We propose new criteria to make EE decisions in DNNs. It combines the confidence score of the intermediary exit classifier to produce an ensemble effect to make PLMs more efficient, robust, and adaptive.

contributions.purpose: Set exit thresholds in a principled way with a guarantee of surpassing vanilla final-layer inference, addressing prior methods' lack of theoretical grounding and strong assumptions (e.g. equal error rate across layers).
contributions.mechanism: Formulate threshold selection as a simple linear program using the error rates of the exit classifiers (Section 3.4); derive a theoretical condition on intermediary-layer error rate under which BEEM provably beats vanilla DNN inference (Section 3.5).
contributions.evaluation: Threshold-setting improves both speed-up and accuracy vs last-layer inference; a condition is derived under which this performance improvement is guaranteed (theoretical).
contributions.source_quote: We provide a method to set threshold values in BEEM by analyzing the error rates of exit classifiers (Section 3.4). This not only helps BEEM achieve better speed-up but also improves accuracy compared to inference at the last layer. We also derive a condition under which this performance is guaranteed.

contributions.purpose: Empirically validate BEEM's speed and accuracy benefits across modalities.
contributions.mechanism: Extensive evaluation on GLUE (PLMs) and COCO (encoder-decoder captioning), comparing against previous EE methods.
contributions.evaluation: Speed-up improvement on both GLUE and COCO; on GLUE accuracy also improves alongside speed-up due to reduced overthinking.
contributions.domain: Efficient inference for language and vision-language tasks
contributions.source_quote: Extensive evaluation showed speed-up improvement in both GLUE and COCO datasets. For the GLUE dataset, accuracy also improves with speedup due to a reduction in the overthinking issues of the DNNs.

self_declared_provenance.quote: EE strategies either perform confidence-based exiting (Xin et al., 2020b; Bajpai & Hanawal, 2024a) or a patience-based exiting (Zhou et al., 2020) ... Recently EEIC (Sun et al., 2021) decided on exiting based on majority voting between the exits. This method also treats each classifier equally. ... They also do not utilize the confidence available from previous layers, thus discarding available information.

We present an EE mechanism named BEEM ... motivated by ensemble learning (Dong et al., 2020), to improve performance of EEDNNs. We treat each intermediate exit classifier as an expert that outputs confidence values on the labels for each input.

notes: Positive framing; BEEM beats prior EE methods on speed and accuracy. Noted trade-off/caveat honestly stated by authors: on harder Image Captioning (COCO) accuracy is only COMPARABLE to the final layer (not an improvement), whereas on easier language tasks it improves -- i.e. the accuracy gain is task-difficulty dependent. Threshold contribution comes with a theoretical guarantee condition (Section 3.5). Speed-up range 1.5x-2.1x.
